In India, the "national song" refers to Vande Mataram (distinct from the national anthem Jana Gana Mana). According to multiple sources, Sri Aurobindo Ghosh translated the national song Vande Mataram into English; his translation was first published on 20th November 1909 [d1][d9]. Sri Aurobindo himself commented on the difficulty of translating the poem, noting its "unique union of sweetness, simple directness and high poetic force" [d2]. Separately, the national anthem Jana Gana Mana was translated into English by Rabindranath Tagore, titled "The Morning Song of India," during his stay at Besant Theosophical College in Madanapalle in 1918 [d3][d5][d6][d7].
